primary_number: 51.29% (life insurance health claims ratio as of April 2025, OJK); 105.7% (AAJI H1 2024 aggregate all-segment); 139.5% (AAJI Q3 2024 aggregate). No primary source confirms 200%+ for any segment or period.
publisher: Antara News, citing Ogi Prastomiyono (Head of OJK Insurance, Guarantee and Pension Fund Supervision) — official OJK statement June 2, 2025
methodology_note: OJK defines the claims ratio as claims paid against gross premiums (premi bruto), explicitly excluding claim reserves and operational expenses. The 51.29% April 2025 figure covers the entire life insurance industry health line, not individual policies in isolation. AAJI H1 2024 figure of 105.7% covers all health insurance within life insurance companies, with individual health claims (Rp 7.62 trillion) separated from group. The 200%+ figure does not appear in OJK statistical releases, AAJI public data, AAUI publications, or any credible trade press citing a named regulator or association. The trustedhealthguides.com source article (the original flagged source) does not actually contain a 200% figure — it discusses rising medical inflation pressuring individual policies without quoting a specific loss ratio. The 200%+ number appears only in AI-generated search summaries and an unverified Mordor Intelligence snippet, both without traceable primary citations.
